============================================================================
GiNaC cross-check oracle for Eichler.jl  (independent of the Julia code)
GiNaC version: 1.8.7   (Walden-Weinzierl arXiv:2010.05271 kernels)
CLN working precision: Digits = 140 decimal digits
All printed values are floating point at that precision; the truncation
cross-checks reported below bound the error far below 1e-100.
============================================================================

Kernel definitions (GiNaC objects):
  E1K1 = Eisenstein_kernel(1,6,1,-3,1,1)
  E1K2 = Eisenstein_kernel(1,6,1,-3,2,1)
  E3K1 = Eisenstein_kernel(3,6,-3,1,1,1)
  E3K2 = Eisenstein_kernel(3,6,-3,1,2,1)
  f3   = modular_form_kernel(3,-3*(Eisenstein_kernel(3,6,-3,1,1,1)-8*Eisenstein_kernel(3,6,-3,1,2,1))*sqrt(3),1)
  f4   = modular_form_kernel(4,324*Eisenstein_kernel(1,6,1,-3,1,1)^4,1)
  1    = basic_log_kernel()  (basic log kernel dq/q)

q-expansions (exact, truncated to the shown order; obtained from
q_expansion_modular_form with a safety margin, since its topmost
coefficient can be incomplete for K>1 kernels):
  E1K1: (1/6) + (1)*q^1 + (1)*q^3 + (1)*q^4 + (2)*q^7 + (1)*q^9 + (1)*q^12 + O(q^13)
  E1K2: (1/6) + (1)*q^2 + (1)*q^6 + (1)*q^8 + O(q^13)
  E3K1: (1)*q^1 + (3)*q^2 + (9)*q^3 + (13)*q^4 + (24)*q^5 + (27)*q^6 + (50)*q^7 + (51)*q^8 + (81)*q^9 + (72)*q^10 + (120)*q^11 + (117)*q^12 + O(q^13)
  E3K2: (1)*q^2 + (3)*q^4 + (9)*q^6 + (13)*q^8 + (24)*q^10 + (27)*q^12 + O(q^13)
  f3  : (-3*sqrt(3))*q^1 + (15*sqrt(3))*q^2 + (-27*sqrt(3))*q^3 + (33*sqrt(3))*q^4 + (-72*sqrt(3))*q^5 + (135*sqrt(3))*q^6 + (-150*sqrt(3))*q^7 + (159*sqrt(3))*q^8 + (-243*sqrt(3))*q^9 + (360*sqrt(3))*q^10 + (-360*sqrt(3))*q^11 + (297*sqrt(3))*q^12 + O(q^13)
  f4  : (1/4) + (6)*q^1 + (54)*q^2 + (222)*q^3 + (438)*q^4 + (756)*q^5 + (1998)*q^6 + (2064)*q^7 + (3510)*q^8 + (6054)*q^9 + (6804)*q^10 + (7992)*q^11 + (16206)*q^12 + O(q^13)

Identity check  -3*sqrt(3)*(E3K1-8*E3K2) == 36*sqrt(3)*(e1^3-e1^2*e2-4*e1*e2^2+4*e2^3)
  difference of q-expansions through q^38: 0

PART 2: iterated integrals I(f3; q), I(1, f3; q), I(1, f4, 1, f3; q)

  base point 0 with tangential base point regularisation (AW prescription).

============================================================================
Notes:
 * 'truncation check' compares iterated_integral with N_trunc=256 vs 320;
   agreement at the <=1e-130 level certifies > 100 correct digits (a printed
   0.0 means the two evaluations are bitwise identical at 140-digit precision).
 * 'sensitivity' compares N_trunc=96 vs 320: a small nonzero difference
   demonstrates that N_trunc is honored and the series has converged.
 * 'adaptive default' compares against iterated_integral(l, qbar) without
   explicit truncation (GiNaC's internal convergence strategy).
 * 'series reconstruction' recomputes each integral from the exact
   q-expansion coefficients by elementary series algebra inside this
   program (a3[n]/n, a3[n]/n^2, and the b4*g convolution), independent
   of GiNaC's iterated_integral code path.
 * All three iterated integrals are given by convergent power series with
   REAL coefficients (times the printed prefactors); no log(qbar) terms
   occur, hence the negative real point qbar_t is unambiguous.
============================================================================
